The **perigee** is the point in the Moon's orbit where it is closest to Earth. The **minimum perigee** (i.e., the smallest possible distance) is approximately:

$$
\text{Minimum perigee} = 356,000 \text{ km}
$$

This value is derived from historical and observational data on the Moon's elliptical orbit.

---

$$

$$

This is the time it takes him to run **42.195 km** (standard marathon distance).

---

### ✅ Step 3: Calculate His Running Speed

$$
\text{Speed} = \frac{42.195 \text{ km}}{2.0275 \text{ hours}} \approx 20.81 \text{ km/h}
$$

---

### ✅ Step 4: Compute Total Time to Cover 356,000 km

$$
\text{Total time} = \frac{356,000 \text{ km}}{20.81 \text{ km/h}} \approx 17,100 \text{ hours}
$$

---

### ✅ Step 5: Round to the Nearest 1,000 Hours

$$
17,100 \text{ hours} \rightarrow \text{Rounded to nearest 1,000 hours} = 17,000 \text{ hours}
$$

Since the question asks for **how many thousand hours**, this becomes:

$$
\frac{17,000}{1,000} = 17
$$

---

### ✅ Final Answer

$$
\boxed{17}
$$
